title: Model weights and parameters: what they mean in practice

videos.script: A model is announced as seven billion parameters, or seventy. {{headline}} The number sounds like a measure of how clever it is. It is something plainer. {{plain}} A parameter is one stored number. The model is nothing but those numbers, and the program that multiplies them. {{numbers}} In this lesson you open the smallest model there is and read its parameters. There are four hundred and thirty-six, and each one is a count. {{toy}} Then you do the arithmetic that decides where a large model can run. Parameters times bytes per parameter is the memory it needs. {{sum}} Seven billion weights at sixteen bits is fourteen gigabytes. At four bits it is three and a half. {{shrink}} That one multiplication tells you whether a model fits on a laptop, and what it costs to make it fit. {{fit}}
